questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a factory's smoke raises asthma rates in nearby patients. What kind of externality is this?

options.misconception: confuses production harm with consumption benefit
ignores the external cost to patients
reverses the sign of the externality

questions.explanation: The smoke imposes a cost on third parties during production, so it is a negative production externality. Private cost alone ignores the harm.
questions.hint: Ask who bears the cost and when it arises.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes that a patient's vaccination protects others in the clinic. What kind of externality is this?

options.misconception: confuses consumption benefit with production harm
ignores the external benefit to others
reverses the sign of the externality

questions.explanation: The vaccination creates a benefit for third parties when consumed, so it is a positive consumption externality. Private benefit alone ignores the spillover.
questions.hint: Ask who gains and when it arises.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Define social cost as private plus external cost
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao asks why social cost exceeds private cost for a polluting factory. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Social cost equals private cost plus external cost, so when production harms patients, social cost exceeds the firm's private cost.

questions.explanation: Social cost includes both the firm's private cost and the external cost imposed on others. With harm, social cost is larger.
questions.hint: Social cost equals private cost plus external cost.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why negative externalities cause overproduction
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a firm ignores a $4 external cost per unit. Why does this lead to overproduction?
questions.explanation: The firm produces where private marginal cost equals price, ignoring the $4 external cost, so output exceeds the social optimum. The value 4 is the ignored external cost.
questions.hint: The firm ignores the external cost in its decision.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao proposes a tax equal to the marginal external cost. What is this tax called?
questions.explanation: A tax set equal to marginal external cost is a Pigouvian or corrective tax. The value 1 marks the concept. It internalises the externality.
questions.hint: The tax equals the marginal external cost.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao observes overproduction due to a negative externality. What welfare loss results?

options.text: A transfer from consumers to producers
No loss, because output is higher
options.misconception: confuses more output with more welfare

options.text: Deadweight loss from units whose social cost exceeds benefit
A gain, because private cost is lower

questions.explanation: Overproduction includes units whose social cost exceeds social benefit, creating deadweight loss. Higher output is not always better.
questions.hint: Compare social cost to social benefit for extra units.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a corrective tax internalises an externality
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao asks how a Pigouvian tax changes a firm's decision. What is the effect?

options.text: It increases the firm's private cost to zero

options.misconception: overstates what a tax can do

options.text: It makes the firm face social cost, reducing output

questions.explanation: The tax adds the external cost to the firm's private cost, so it now faces social cost and reduces output toward the optimum.
questions.hint: The tax aligns private cost with social cost.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: External benefits that grow with use
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a health app becomes more valuable as more patients join. What is this?

options.text: A positive externality that grows with use

questions.explanation: When benefits grow with the number of users, the externality is positive and increasing with use. Private benefit alone ignores the spillover.
questions.hint: Benefits rise with the number of users.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why private cost is below social cost
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao asks why a polluting factory's private cost is below social cost. Explain.

answer.exemplar: The factory's private cost excludes the harm to patients, so social cost, which adds that external cost, is larger.

questions.explanation: Private cost omits external harm. Social cost adds it, making social cost larger than private cost.
questions.hint: Social cost equals private plus external cost.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why positive consumption externalities cause underconsumption
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a vaccine's social benefit exceeds its private benefit by $6. Why does this lead to underconsumption?
questions.explanation: Consumers buy based on private benefit, ignoring the $6 external benefit, so consumption falls below the social optimum. The value 6 is the ignored external benefit.
questions.hint: Consumers ignore the external benefit.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute social cost from private and external costs
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao records private cost $10 and external cost $3 per unit. What is social cost per unit?
questions.explanation: Social cost is private cost plus external cost: 10 plus 3 equals 13. The common slip is to use private cost alone.
questions.hint: Add private and external costs.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the result of ignoring external costs
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao observes a factory producing where private marginal cost equals price. What is the problem?

options.text: There is no problem if profit is positive
Output is below the social optimum
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the error

options.text: Output exceeds the social optimum because external cost is ignored

options.misconception: blames price rather than the externality

questions.explanation: Ignoring external cost makes the firm produce too much. The social optimum requires social marginal cost to equal price.
questions.hint: Compare private and social marginal cost.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: State the size of a Pigouvian tax

options.misconception: uses average cost instead of external cost

options.text: Equal to the marginal external cost

questions.explanation: A Pigouvian tax equals marginal external cost. It internalises the externality without needing to know profit or price.
questions.hint: The tax matches the marginal external cost.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain the source of deadweight loss
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao observes deadweight loss from a negative externality. What creates it?

options.text: Units not produced that would be profitable
Units produced whose social cost exceeds social benefit

questions.explanation: Deadweight loss arises from units whose social cost exceeds social benefit. Tax revenue is a transfer, not a loss.
questions.hint: Compare social cost to social benefit for extra units.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS

answer.exemplar: The tax makes the firm pay the external cost, so its private cost becomes social cost and it reduces output to the optimum.

questions.explanation: Internalisation means the decision-maker bears the external cost. The tax achieves this by adding it to private cost.
questions.hint: The decision-maker bears the external cost.

questions.explanation: Overproduction includes units whose social cost exceeds social benefit, creating deadweight loss. Higher output is not always better.
questions.hint: Compare social cost to social benefit for extra units.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a corrective tax internalises an externality
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao asks how a Pigouvian tax changes a firm's decision. What is the effect?

options.text: It increases the firm's private cost to zero

options.misconception: overstates what a tax can do

options.text: It makes the firm face social cost, reducing output

questions.explanation: The tax adds the external cost to the firm's private cost, so it now faces social cost and reduces output toward the optimum.
questions.hint: The tax aligns private cost with social cost.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: External benefits that grow with use
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a vaccination registry becomes more valuable as more clinics join. What is this?

options.text: A positive externality that grows with use

questions.explanation: When benefits grow with the number of users, the externality is positive and increasing with use. Private benefit alone ignores the spillover.
questions.hint: Benefits rise with the number of users.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why private cost is below social cost
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao asks why a polluting factory's private cost is below social cost. Explain.

answer.exemplar: The factory's private cost excludes the harm to patients, so social cost, which adds that external cost, is larger.

questions.explanation: Private cost omits external harm. Social cost adds it, making social cost larger than private cost.
questions.hint: Social cost equals private plus external cost.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao notes a vaccine's social benefit exceeds private benefit by $10. Why does this lead to underconsumption?
questions.explanation: Consumers buy based on private benefit, ignoring the $10 external benefit, so consumption falls below the social optimum. The value 10 is the ignored external benefit.
questions.hint: Consumers ignore the external benefit.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao records private cost $16 and external cost $5 per unit. What is social cost per unit?
questions.explanation: Social cost is private cost plus external cost: 16 plus 5 equals 21. The common slip is to use private cost alone.
questions.hint: Add private and external costs.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Clinician Dr. Rao observes a market with negative production externalities. What is the typical output outcome?

options.text: Underproduction relative to the social optimum
Overproduction relative to the social optimum

questions.explanation: Negative production externalities lead to overproduction because firms ignore external costs. The market output exceeds the social optimum.
questions.hint: Firms ignore external costs when deciding output.
